Four snare drums and three drum kits, each drawn and played from one physical model. Pick any two, tune one, hear both, and translate the tuning to the other. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn what shapes a drum's sound: the head's modes, where you hit it, the shell, the heads, the snare wires, muffling.
2. Click a drawing to strike the centre, the edge or the rim; tune it with its keys; throw the snares off.
3. Translate a tuning from one drum or kit to another and see what carries over and what is lost.
:::

## What shapes a drum's sound

- **Modes**: an ideal round head vibrates at the zeros of the Bessel functions (Wikipedia, "Vibrations of a circular membrane"): 1, 1.59, 2.14, 2.30… times the lowest, not a harmonic series. The air in the shell pulls these closer together (physics texts say so; none read for this page, so the amount is the site's: unverified).
- **Pitch**: tighter is higher; wider is lower at the same tension. A 14" snare's batter is usually tuned 220-349 Hz, its bottom head a fifth or so higher (Wikipedia, "Drum tuning").
- **Where you hit it**: the centre sounds mostly the round modes; the edge many more (more ring); a rimshot adds the rim's crack; a cross-stick is the rim alone.
- **Snare wires**: they rattle on the bottom head; the throw-off lifts them and the drum sounds like a tom (Wikipedia, "Snare drum"). The strainer knob sets how tight they are.
- **Shell and heads**: metal shells ring, wood is warmer, a two-ply or calf-style head is shorter and fatter (drummers' lore; the numbers are the site's).
- **Muffling and the port**: muffles deaden ring and overtones (Wikipedia, "Drum kit"); a hole in the kick's front head (about 6") gives a less round, shorter boom (Wikipedia, "Drum tuning").

## Two side by side

Choose a snare or kit for each side. **Click a drum** in the drawing (centre / edge / rim), or use the buttons; **▶ Groove** plays a short beat. The spectrum under each shows the last hit and its centroid (higher = brighter).

```{=html}
<div class="dkc" data-cat="snare" data-a="supraphonic" data-b="blackbeauty"></div>
```

## Translating a tuning

**Translate** carries the tuning over by pitch: each drum's lowest mode is matched on the other drum (if it can reach it), and the wires, strainer, muffling, head and port go with it. The report says **exact**, **approx** (shell, size or depth differ) or **lost** (more than 4 semitones out of reach). A snare can go into a kit's snare stand and back. Try the rock kit into the jazz kit: the 18" kick cannot get down to the 22"'s boom.

## What is this site's own

- Every number of the model (pitch bases, decay times, shell partials, wire noise, strike radii, the air-loading exponent), the four snares' sizes, lugs and finishes, the kits' shells and cymbal choices. The drawings are after photos, not measured; no makers' logos.
- Nobody has compared the sound with real drums.

## Works Cited

"Drum kit." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_kit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_kit). Usual sizes (22" bass drum most common; 12"/13" toms, 14"/16" floor), hi-hat, ride 20", crash 16"; muffles deaden ring and overtones.

"Drum tuning." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_tuning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_tuning). 14" snare batter 220-349 Hz, resonant head 330-391 Hz, most often a fifth above; bass drum front head port about 6", less "round"; muffling.

"Gretsch." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gretsch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gretsch). Founded 1883 in Brooklyn; a drum company first (the article's drum section is empty: the round-badge era is not described there).

"Ludwig Drums." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Drums). Founded 1909; Ringo Starr on Ed Sullivan 1964; notable artists list (Al Jackson Jr., Clyde Stubblefield, Carlton Barrett, John Bonham, Joe Morello, Roger Taylor, Mick Fleetwood...).

McLean, Scott, et al. "SM Drums (Deeply Sampled Free Drums)." SFZ edition, sfzinstruments, GitHub, accessed 27 Nov. 2026. The cymbal recordings the pages play (cymbal-samples/*.m4a). Its manual: "A Zildjian series" cymbals, 14" New Beat hats, 20" Ping and 17" Thin rides, 13/15/16/17" crashes, a Wuhan 15" china. Terms, the authors' site as quoted on KVR: free royalty free use by anyone for anything.

"Snare drum." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum). Two heads, snares on the bottom head, a lever on the strainer throws them off (then it sounds like a tom); rimshots; kit snares 14" x 5-8"; piccolo 13-14" across, about 4" or less, higher.

"Vibrations of a circular membrane." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrations_of_a_circular_membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrations_of_a_circular_membrane). Modes of an ideal drum head at the zeros of the Bessel functions J_m.

"Vistalite." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vistalite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vistalite). Ludwig's acrylic drums, from 1972, popularised by John Bonham; reissued 2001 (amber Bonham replica).
